Flush below then strong reclaim that holds would confirm. If lose 76 and reject, stay patient. First target $100, $76 start buying, $65 load more. Need clean setup with defined risk.
text:
$AAOI Trade Idea: Nov 27 90C

Trigger: 76 ✅
Targets: 93, 100 🎯
Stop: 70 🛑

$AAOI has lost 67% of its value since its May 13th all-time high.

Now it’s approaching a level that has my attention: $76.

A massive drawdown doesn’t automatically make a stock cheap.

I want to see buyers step in and defend support.

Here’s my plan: 

Watching $76 for selling to slow and a base to form.

A flush below $76 followed by a strong reclaim would get my attention.

I want to see that reclaim HOLD.

From there, I’m looking for a higher low and a break above the bounce high to confirm buyers are gaining control.

If we lose $76 and keep rejecting it from below, I’ll stay patient.

Support can become resistance.

On a confirmed setup, I’d define my invalidation below the setup low and size accordingly.

First target is $100, taking partials and leaving a runner if momentum follows.

I don’t need to catch the exact bottom.

I need a clean setup with defined risk. 

$76 is the level to start buying.

$65 is where I would load up more.

en_summary: @MebFaber podcast: by Citi's math we have been in a bubble since mid last year, and Dirk Willer says keep buying; topics include why 1929 is the only bubble that crashed immediately, why the bond selloff is about growth not deficits, and gold peaking when the PBOC stops buying.
text:
By @Citi's math, we’ve been in a bubble since mid last year, and Dirk Willer, Head of Global Macro Asset Allocation, says to keep buying.

We also cover:

• Why 1929 is the only bubble that crashed immediately
• The Warsh shadow rate and why it tracked Greenspan’s Fed
• Why the bond selloff is about growth and not deficits
• Why Brazil’s 9% to 10% real rates set up a big opportunity
• Why gold peaks when the PBOC is done buying
• His favorite bubble hedge
